result:
Grades for `submissions/s1.json` on quiz 0001 are written to `grades/0001-s1.json`, after two review passes (one fix each pass — adding a genuine credit to the q4 feedback, then breaking up three dense paragraphs into shorter sentences per your preferences).

**Summary:** Riley nailed the agent loop itself (q1) and the stopping-condition idea for a stuck agent (q3). The recurring gap is who actually runs a tool — twice (q2, the calendar check; q4, counting model calls) the answer had the model executing the tool itself in one step, when really it only requests the tool and the program runs it. Partial credit on q5 (missing the "why" of sending a result back) and q6 (right on tool selection, but added a false claim that the model remembers past sessions on its own).

**Next step:** have Riley trace one makerspace request call-by-call, labeling each line as "model requests" vs. "program executes" vs. "model continues," before the next lesson on context and memory — which should make that split explicit up front so the memory lesson doesn't reinforce the same "it just remembers" instinct.
